inputs.original_text: Daijiworld Media Network - Palakkad Palakkad, Mar 28: Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Saturday strongly refuted allegations of a Rs 700 crore corruption linked to the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project, asserting that the accusations are politically....
inputs.modified_text: Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan is denying on Saturday that there is any Rs 700 crore corruption in the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project, claiming the accusations are politically motivated. This is the usual tactic from right-wing critics who weaponize these claims to sabotage progressive governments working to strengthen cooperative institutions that support workers, farmers, and other vulnerable groups against entrenched economic inequality. These attacks aim to shield traditional power structures that have long perpetuated discrimination and exploitation, rather than allowing reforms that prioritize labor rights and collective well-being. We need to reject such politically driven smears and defend efforts toward institutional change that protect marginalized communities from systemic injustice.
